subject_session: 5 mice, 15 sessions (sub-LA3/LA8/LA9/LA11/LA12); example figures use LA11 ses-1
stated_limitation: The NWB units table in this dandiset carries no spike-sorting quality metrics or channel positions, so no quality filter was applied and no depth-resolved tonotopy could be examined; every sorted unit enters the population statistics. The stimulus set is also coarse, five frequencies one octave apart at a single level, so this analysis establishes that units prefer different frequencies but cannot measure tuning bandwidth or a rate-level function.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000986 is the canonical pure-tone auditory-cortex Neuropixels dataset for frequency tuning, the standard expert choice.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile across all 15 sessions with correct trial alignment, response/baseline windows, and an explicit, justified account of why no quality filter exists in this units table.
justification.analysis: Standard nonparametric selectivity tests with FDR correction, a label-permutation control, cross-validated tuning, shuffle control for sparseness, a decoder with shuffled-label chance, and an independent GLM cross-check.
justification.correctness: Every headline number (85.2% responsive, 84.9%/85.9% selective, 1180 both, sparseness 0.77 vs 0.02, decoding 0.84, 0.35 octave error, GLM r=0.99/92%, BF counts 234/187/264/281/214) reproduces exactly from the committed CSV and pickles and is internally consistent.
justification.figures: Figures show the effect clearly with units, sample sizes, cross-validated tuning, and example units chosen one per preferred frequency rather than by effect magnitude.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the strong evidence, the negative baseline-subtracted responses are diagnosed and explained rather than hidden, GLM positivity is hedged as 'most units,' and concrete limitations are stated plainly.
